Florida Homestead Exemption · Amendment 3

Florida's larger homestead exemption has one deadline that matters

Under Amendment 3, Florida's homestead exemption grows substantially — but only for homeowners whose permanent residence is Florida in time. If Florida is going to be your home, the date below decides whether you qualify for the larger exemption.

Permanent Residency Deadline
December 31, 2026

Florida must be your PERMANENT RESIDENCE by this date.

Read that carefully: the test is permanent residency by December 31, 2026 — not simply buying a home, and not simply owning one by that date. A second home, an investment property, or a house you have closed on but have not made your permanent home does not meet the test.

The larger exemption

Homeowners who meet the December 31, 2026 permanent residency deadline are in line for the expanded exemption:

$150,000
In 2027

The homestead exemption rises to $150,000 for qualifying permanent residents.

$250,000
In 2028

The exemption climbs again, to $250,000, the following year.

$50,000

New to Florida? New Florida residents receive a $50,000 phase-in exemption as they establish permanent residency.

What this means if you are buying

If you plan to make Florida your permanent home, closing on your home and establishing permanent residency before December 31, 2026 is what puts you in line for the larger exemption. Buying alone is not enough — Florida has to actually be your permanent residence by that date. Then there is one more step:

  1. 1

    Close and move in before the deadline. Your purchase should close, and Florida should be your permanent residence, by December 31, 2026.

  2. 2

    File for the exemption. Submit your homestead exemption filing with your county property appraiser by March 1, 2027.

  3. 3

    The larger exemption applies. Qualifying homeowners receive the $150,000 exemption in 2027, rising to $250,000 in 2028.

Key dates

Dec 31, 2026
Permanent residency deadline — Florida must be your permanent residence by this date to qualify for the larger exemption.
Mar 1, 2027
First filing deadline — file for the exemption with your county property appraiser.
2027
$150,000 exemption for qualifying permanent residents.
2028
$250,000 exemption — the exemption rises to its full amount.
